items.title: 谷歌确认原生“应用锁”功能无法通过 Google Play 推送至旧版安卓设备，需升级至安卓 17 QPR3
items.description: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，随着谷歌近年来逐渐通过独立更新向用户推送 Android 新功能，部分用户希望无需升级至最新版 Android，也能通过更新 Google Play 获得最新“应用锁”功能。 不过谷歌员工 Mishaal Rahman 在 Reddit 确认，Android 原生应用锁功能不会通过 Google Play 系统更新推送至旧版 Android 设备，相应功能依赖操作系统底层 API 支持，将于 2027 年第一季度随 Android 17 QPR3 正式版推出，安卓原生用户必须为自己的设备更新最新系统才能获得相应功能。 不过这并不意味着旧版 Android 手机永远无法获得原生应用锁，事实上包括小米等厂商多年来就早已在自家系统中提供类似功能，用户可以通过指纹、PIN 码、图案或密码验证才能打开受保护的应用。

items.content: 今天，知名半导体和 AI 研究机构 SemiAnalysis 在 X 上发了一张写给 Google DeepMind 主席 Demis Hassabis 的《向 Google 道歉专用表》。 理由一栏勾了包括「我只看了 X 上大家的消息」、「我那在 Anthropic 工作的室友，说服我相信 Gemini 已经完了」和「我没有阅读模型卡」等原因。最有意思的是最后一行：「Demis，关于 Gemini 4，我们错了。我们只想撤回一个词。」 他们从自己当初的标题里划掉了一个 is：Gemini is cooked。一句「Gemini 完了」，变成了「Gemini 这回真做出了点东西」。 事件的起因是 SemiAnalysis 在今年 8 月份发布了一篇文章，通篇都在讲 Google 自从去年 11 月短暂领先之后，就再也没有发布任何让人激动的模型，几乎是处在了掉队中的状态。 当时他们分析 DeepMind 的强化学习团队走了不少人，内部的算力又没分配好，对 Google 下了一个相当重的判断： 照这样下去，Google 当然还会继续发模型，但再一次达到行业最高水平的概率，已经「降到了零」。 报告发出不到两个月，谷歌就公布了 Gemini 4 Argon，接着 10 月底发布 Carbon、11 月 12 号推出 Hydrogen，18 号发布 Neon，短短 8 天的时间，接连推出了 3 款模型，其中 Carbon 的表现当时还来到了 Artificial Analysis 的综合能力榜首。

items.content: 《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）首批媒体评测于 11 月 18 日公开。据《综艺》当天报道，游戏在 Metacritic 获得 99 分，追平 1998 年 N64 版《塞尔达传说：时之笛》的平台历史最高分。Rockstar 官网确认，游戏于 11 月 19 日登陆 PS5 和 Xbox Series X|S。 The Verge 的评测在接近 80 小时体验后，肯定了杰森与露西娅的双主角关系，以及与开放世界玩法结合的叙事。故事设定在以佛罗里达州为原型的 Leonida，玩家可分别扮演两人，并逐步建立他们的关系；除主线任务外，也可通过不同活动探索罪恶都市、海滩和沼泽等地区。 该评测使用首发版 PS5，称整体运行良好，但也提到战斗操作仍显笨重、武器轮盘容易误选，以及少量物理和道具显示错误。完成主线并游玩超过 70 小时后，评测者的总进度仍不足 60%。 谷歌 11 月 18 日发布 Gemini 4 Neon，面向软件开发、知识工作和科学研究，开始向 Gemini API、Gemini for business、Antigravity 及 Gemini 应用开放。其中，Gemini 应用和 Antigravity 面向 Google AI Pro、Ultra 订阅用户。 Neon 支持 100 万 Token 上下文，可综合处理电子表格、PDF、图表、音频和视频。API 每百万输入 Token 收费 3 美元、输出收费 15 美元，缓存输入为 0.15 美元。谷歌称，在默认 high 思考档位下，Neon 在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 保持较高能力的同时，单任务成本比 Carbon 低 32%。 模型可独立完成多步骤任务，也能在 Antigravity 中调度 Hydrogen 子智能体。按谷歌公布的测试，Neon 在 xhigh 档位的 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 得分为 61，位列第三；在默认 high 档位的 FrontierCode 2.0 测试中得分为 46.2%。

items.content: 所以判断一门影像手艺成没成，有个简单粗暴的试金石：敢不敢上大银幕。胶片当年闯过这关，数字摄影机也闯过，三维动画同样闯过，每闯过一关，就意味着一项新技术拿到了成熟影像工业的入场券。 过去两年，AI 视频生成你方唱罢我登场，一个比一个惊艳，可真正到了商业制作的修罗场，甲方要的是原生 4K，导演想一镜到底，品牌方动不动就改需求，制作团队还得在成本、周期和最终交付之间走钢丝。 最近，爱范儿注意到即梦 Seedance 2.5 推出了 4K 版本，把最长 30 秒单次生成、全模态参考、视频编辑与延长等本领一并拉到了更高的画质规格。 过去体验 AI 视频模型，我总习惯给它安排一些足够热闹的场面。巨型怪兽、千军万马、末日都市，最好再来点爆炸与运镜，十几秒的视频也能拍出大片预告的气势。 但仔细想想，真正让商业制作团队头疼的，可能是一瓶香水上的标签、一张在不同渠道反复使用的商品图，或者导演临时要求修改的某个镜头。 假设客户要拍一条高端机械腕表广告，镜头从表盘的极近距离开始，掠过钻石时标和日期窗口，最后缓缓后退，露出放在私人书房里的完整腕表。

The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.” “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting says. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.” The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move “fluidly between tools” and “carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.” TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response. Agents capable of computer work have become one of the hottest commodities in the tech industry over the past year. Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have launched such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space. It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to expand its AI offerings in the new John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.

items.content: Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of them ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece to sell in the IPO. At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for. Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy. However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.” With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting. $104.8 billion. items.title: Meta’s new Muse Charm device may cost $300
items.description: Meta hasn't denied the reporting from The Information, saying only that it will "have more to share soon" about its upcoming AI wearable.
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the company’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported . When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.” So far, Meta has made a relatively successful push into consumer AI, launching Muse — its agentic helper — along with a variety of cute avatars that users can use to give the system more of a personality. Muse Charm, the company’s push into AI hardware, will allow users to carry a physical personification of its software around in their pocket (or potentially wear it around their neck), talking to it, asking it questions, and giving it commands. It remains to be seen whether customers will bite or not. AI wearables have had a rough go of it so far (here’s looking at you, Humane Ai pin ), but companies continue to iterate on the concept in an attempt to break through to a broader audience. Indeed, $300 is arguably a pretty steep price for a product the size of a keychain, although it’s also a price point that’s in line with what other companies have been charging. items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.description: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
